Reduce the dose of maraviroc to 150 mg twice daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, as conjugated estrogens can increase maraviroc levels by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely due to the potential for increased toxicity. 2. Vaginal conjugated estrogens also increase maraviroc levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for signs of toxicity. 3. Cortisone decreases maraviroc levels or effects by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Crizotinib increases maraviroc levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction of maraviroc may be necessary. Monitor closely. 5. Crofelemer increases maraviroc levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 in the gut. However, systemic inhibition is unlikely due to minimal absorption. Use caution and monitor. 6. Cyclosporine increases maraviroc levels or effects by both inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 7. Dabrafenib decreases maraviroc levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 8. Danazol increases maraviroc levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 9. Danicopan increases maraviroc levels or effects by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. It also increases plasma concentrations of P-gp substrates, necessitating dose reduction of sensitive P-gp substrates to avoid serious adverse reactions. Use caution and monitor. 10. Darifenacin increases maraviroc levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 11. Darunavir increases maraviroc levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 12. Dasatinib increases maraviroc levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 13. Deferasirox decreases maraviroc levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 14. Maraviroc increases desipramine levels or effects by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 15. Dexamethasone decreases maraviroc levels or effects by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 16. Herbal DHEA increases maraviroc levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 17. Dienogest/estradiol valerate increases maraviroc levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for potential toxicity. 18. Diltiazem increases maraviroc levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 19. Maraviroc and doxazosin may enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Use caution and monitor. 20. Dronedarone increases maraviroc levels or effects by inhibiting both CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 21. Maraviroc increases duloxetine levels or effects by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 22. Duvelisib increases maraviroc levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Co-administration with duvelisib increases the AUC of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates, potentially increasing toxicity risks. Dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates should be considered. 23. Efavirenz decreases maraviroc levels or effects by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 24. Elagolix increases maraviroc levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and decreases maraviroc levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 25. Eliglustat increases maraviroc levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 26. Maraviroc and enalapril may enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Use caution and monitor. 27. Encorafenib affects maraviroc metabolism by both inhibiting and inducing CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Co-administration may result in increased toxicity or decreased efficacy of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. Use caution and monitor. 28. Maraviroc and eprosartan may enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Use caution and monitor. 29. Erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, and stearate forms) increases maraviroc levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 30. Eslicarbazepine acetate decreases maraviroc levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 31. Maraviroc and esmolol may enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Use caution and monitor. 32. Conjugated synthetic estrogens increase maraviroc levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism, with a potential for increased toxicity. Use caution and monitor. 33. Esterified estrogens increase maraviroc levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, with a potential for increased toxicity. Use caution and monitor. 34. Estropipate increases maraviroc levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism, with a potential for increased toxicity. Use caution and monitor. 35. Maraviroc and ethacrynic acid may enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor. 36. Etonogestrel increases maraviroc levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism, with a potential for increased toxicity. Use caution and monitor. 37. Etravirine decreases maraviroc levels or effects by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 38. Etynodiol increases maraviroc levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism, with a potential for increased toxicity. Use caution and monitor. 39. Fedratinib increases maraviroc levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as necessary. Use caution and monitor. 40. Felodipine increases maraviroc levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 41. Maraviroc and fenoldopam may enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Use caution and monitor. 42. Maraviroc increases flecainide levels or effects by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 43. Fluconazole increases maraviroc levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 44. Fludrocortisone decreases maraviroc levels or effects by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 45. Fluvoxamine increases maraviroc levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 46. Fosamprenavir increases maraviroc levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce maraviroc dose to 150 mg twice daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Maraviroc decreases the conversion of fosamprenavir to its active form, amprenavir. Use caution and monitor. 47. Fosaprepitant increases maraviroc levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 48. Maraviroc and fosinopril may enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Use caution and monitor. 49. Fosphenytoin decreases maraviroc levels or effects by influencing both CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 50. Maraviroc and furosemide may enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor. 51. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases maraviroc levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 52. Grapefruit increases maraviroc levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 53. Griseofulvin decreases maraviroc levels or effects by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 54. Maraviroc increases haloperidol levels or effects by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 55. Maraviroc increases hydrocodone levels or effects by altering CYP2D6 metabolism. Hydromorphone, a minor metabolite of hydrocodone, is formed via CYP2D6-mediated O-demethylation and may contribute to the total analgesic effect of hydrocodone. Use caution and monitor. 56. Hydrocortisone decreases maraviroc levels or effects by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 57. Maraviroc increases hydromorphone levels or effects by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 58. Maraviroc increases iloperidone levels or effects by altering CYP2D6 metabolism, while iloperidone increases maraviroc levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may increase plasma levels of drugs predominantly metabolized by CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor. 59. Imatinib increases maraviroc levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust maraviroc dose to 150 mg twice daily. Use caution and monitor for potential toxicity. 60. Maraviroc increases imipramine levels or effects by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 61. Maraviroc and indapamide may enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Use caution and monitor. 62. Indinavir increases maraviroc levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism and inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Reduce maraviroc dose to 150 mg twice daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Use caution and monitor. 63. Maraviroc and irbesartan may enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Use caution and monitor. 64. Maraviroc and isocarboxazid may enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Use caution and monitor. 65. Isoniazid increases maraviroc levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce maraviroc dose to 150 mg twice daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Use caution and monitor. 66. Maraviroc and isosorbide dinitrate may enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Use caution and monitor. 67. Maraviroc and isosorbide mononitrate may enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Use caution and monitor. 68. Maraviroc and isradipine may enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Use caution and monitor. 69. Istradefylline increases maraviroc levels or effects by inhibiting both CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. At 40 mg/day, istradefylline increased peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 and P-gp substrates in clinical trials. Dose reduction of sensitive substrates should be considered. Use caution and monitor. 70. Itraconazole increases maraviroc levels or effects by inhibiting both CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Reduce maraviroc dose to 150 mg twice daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 71. Ivacaftor increases maraviroc levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Ivacaftor and its M1 metabolite may significantly increase systemic exposure to sensitive P-gp substrates with a narrow therapeutic index. Use caution and monitor. 72. Ketoconazole increases maraviroc levels or effects by inhibiting both CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Reduce maraviroc dose to 150 mg twice daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Use caution and monitor. 73. Maraviroc and labetalol may enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of orthostatic hypotension. Use caution and monitor. 74. Lapatinib increases maraviroc levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor.
